title: Sandbag each light stand on the leg under its boom
instruction: Weight both light stands with the red sandbags, one bag per stand, following set convention: lay each bag flat and lengthwise along the leg directly under that stand's yellow boom, its centre 7 to 13 cm out from the post.
context: Set convention for a stand carrying a boom is to put the sandbag on the leg under the boom, the side the load hangs over; a bag on another leg is the rookie mistake a key grip corrects, because a stand that tips drops a hot, heavy light onto the crew. Done by: lighting technicians, grips, stagehands.
setup: World frame from the robot: forward is away from the arm bases, left and right as the robot sees them. Two light stands are fixed to the table, one in front of each arm. Each has a black round post (aluminium tube, 30 mm diameter, 38 cm tall), three dark grey legs (steel flat bars 16 cm long, 40 mm wide, 20 mm tall, lying on the table, each starting at the post's surface so it ends 17.5 cm from the post's centre, 120 degrees apart) and a yellow boom stub (painted wood, 45 mm long, 20 x 20 mm in section) fixed to the post's side at the very top (its top flush with the post's top), sticking out over one leg and ending 6 cm from the post's centre. Left stand: post centre 40 cm forward of the left arm's base and in line with it (30.5 cm left of the centre line); one leg points straight back toward the arms, the other two point forward-left and forward-right, each 60 degrees from straight forward; the boom points straight back toward the arms, over the backward leg. Right stand: post centre 30 cm forward of the right arm's base and 10 cm further right than it (40.5 cm right of the centre line); one leg points straight left toward the centre line, the other two point back-right and forward-right, each 60 degrees from straight right (30 degrees from straight back and straight forward); the boom points left, toward the centre line, over the left-pointing leg. Two red sandbags, each a rigid, closed plastic box 70 x 50 x 35 mm, a stand-in for a shot bag, filled with steel shot (about 85 cm3 of it, the rest packed with foam so the shot can't shift) and weighed to 400 g (sand or wood can't reach 400 g at this size: sand fills it to about 200 g), lie flat on the table 17 cm forward of the arm bases, 12 cm left and 12 cm right of the centre line, long sides pointing forward. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored per stand, either bag counting. 0.35 for a bag lying on the leg under the stand's boom: resting on one of its 70 x 50 mm faces (either one, so upside down counts), not on a side or end face, within 10 degrees of level; its lowest point touching the leg's top (1.5 mm above to 3 mm below it, the leg's top being 20 mm above the table); its centre within 20 mm of the leg's centre line and 70 to 130 mm out from the post's centre along the leg. Plus 0.15 if that bag's long side is within 20 degrees of the leg's direction. Both stands, both bags lengthwise: 1.0. 0 for a stand with no such bag (a bag on the table, held or hanging more than 1.5 mm above the leg, stacked on the other bag, wedged between two legs, resting on a 70 x 35 or 50 x 35 mm face, or with its centre outside 70 to 130 mm). 0 overall if any bag lies on a leg that is not under a boom (its lowest point within 1.5 mm above to 3 mm below that leg's top and its centre within 20 mm of that leg's centre line, anywhere along it). A bag still in the gripper counts if its lowest point is within the 1.5 mm above to 3 mm below band; the score does not check release. Scored at the last step; the trial ends early at 1.0 once both stands earn full credit and both bags are still (moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 radians a second) for 2.5 s.
reset_notes: Lay both bags back flat on the table 17 cm forward of the arm bases, one 12 cm left and one 12 cm right of the centre line, long sides pointing forward. The stands are clamped or screwed to the table and don't move; check that no bag was left on a leg.
fidelity: Approximate: a real sandbag is floppy and drapes over a leg; here it is a rigid box, so it can sit crosswise on the 40 mm leg. The stands are scale models fixed to the table, so nothing tips: the score checks the set convention (bag on the leg under the boom), not a tipping calculation. Every object, the stands included, has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
